Title: "The Iron Maiden"

INT. DARK, DINGY BASEMENT - NIGHT

A dimly lit, damp basement. The air is thick with the stench of mold and decay. The only sound is the dripping of water from a leaky pipe.

In the center of the room, a large, imposing iron maiden stands ominously. Its spiked exterior gleams in the flickering light of a single, guttering candle.

At one end of the room, a man, JAX, is tied to a chair. His face is bruised and swollen, his eyes blackened. He is barely conscious.

At the other end of the room, a figure emerges from the shadows. It is KAIN, a tall, gaunt man with a cruel, twisted face. He wears a long, black coat and carries a leather-bound book.

KAIN: (sneering) Ah, you're finally awake. I was beginning to think you'd never regain consciousness.

JAX: (groaning) What do you want from me?

KAIN: (laughs) Patience, my dear prisoner. I want the truth. The location of the hidden treasure.

JAX: (spitting blood) You'll never get it.

KAIN: (grabbing a pair of pliers from a nearby table) I think you'll find that I'm quite resourceful.

He approaches Jax, the pliers clinking ominously.

KAIN: (leaning in close) Tell me where it is, and I'll make this as painless as possible. Refuse, and I'll make you wish for death.

JAX: (laughs bitterly) You're insane.

KAIN: (smiling) Perhaps. But I've grown quite fond of this little game we're playing.

He grabs a handful of Jax's hair and yanks his head back, exposing his neck.

KAIN: (whispering) Now, tell me the truth.

JAX: (gritting his teeth) I don't know where it is.

KAIN: (disappointed) Lies. Very well.

He stands up and walks back to the iron maiden. He opens the book and begins to read from it.

KAIN: (reciting) "By the power of the ancient texts, I command thee, iron maiden, to inflict pain upon this wretched soul."

As he finishes the incantation, the iron maiden begins to creak and groan. Its spikes extend outwards, ready to strike.

JAX: (screaming) No! Please, I'll tell you anything!

FADE OUT.
